example.romaji: shigoto no ato no biiru wa saikou
example.ja: 仕事のあとのビールは最高
example.english: Beer after work is the best.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto no ato no biiru wa saikou desu
examplePolite.ja: 仕事のあとのビールは最高です
examplePolite.english: A beer after work is the best.

notes: At a bar, nama or nama biiru is draft beer.

example.romaji: aka wain to shiro, dotchi ga ii?
example.ja: 赤ワインと白、どっちがいい?
example.english: Red wine or white, which do you want?

examplePolite.romaji: aka wain to shiro, dochira ga ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 赤ワインと白、どちらがいいですか?
examplePolite.english: Would you prefer red wine or white?

use: Covers sweet soft drinks like cola too, not just fruit juice.

example.romaji: kodomo ni wa juusu de ii?
example.ja: 子どもにはジュースでいい?
example.english: Is juice okay for the kids?

examplePolite.romaji: kodomo ni wa juusu de ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 子どもにはジュースでいいですか?
examplePolite.english: Is juice all right for the children?

example.romaji: tanjoubi no keeki katte kita yo
example.ja: 誕生日のケーキ買ってきたよ
example.english: I picked up a birthday cake.

examplePolite.romaji: tanjoubi no keeki o katte kimashita
examplePolite.ja: 誕生日のケーキを買ってきました
examplePolite.english: I bought a birthday cake.

use: Covers candy, chips and biscuits, anything packaged to snack on.

example.romaji: okashi bakkari tabenai no
example.ja: お菓子ばっかり食べないの
example.english: Stop eating nothing but snacks.

examplePolite.romaji: okashi bakari tabenaide kudasai
examplePolite.ja: お菓子ばかり食べないでください
examplePolite.english: Please don't eat only snacks.

use: Means ice cream, not ice; ice cubes are koori.

example.romaji: atsui kara aisu tabetai
example.ja: 暑いからアイス食べたい
example.english: It's so hot, I want ice cream.

examplePolite.romaji: atsui node aisu ga tabetai desu
examplePolite.ja: 暑いのでアイスが食べたいです
examplePolite.english: It's hot, so I'd like some ice cream.

notes: Before a drink it means iced: aisu koohii.

use: Short for chokoreeto; the short form is what people usually say.

example.romaji: sono choko ikko moratte ii?
example.ja: そのチョコ一個もらっていい?
example.english: Can I have one of those chocolates?

examplePolite.romaji: sono choko ikko moratte mo ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: そのチョコ一個もらってもいいですか?
examplePolite.english: May I have one of those chocolates?

notes: On Valentine's Day women give choko; giri choko is the obligation chocolate for coworkers.

use: The afternoon snack between meals, especially for kids.

example.romaji: oyatsu ni purin aru yo
example.ja: おやつにプリンあるよ
example.english: There's pudding for a snack.

examplePolite.romaji: oyatsu ni purin ga arimasu yo
examplePolite.ja: おやつにプリンがありますよ
examplePolite.english: There's some pudding for a snack.

use: Usually Japanese curry over rice, a standard home dinner.

example.romaji: kyou no bangohan karee da yo
example.ja: 今日の晩ご飯カレーだよ
example.english: We're having curry for dinner tonight.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou no bangohan wa karee desu
examplePolite.ja: 今日の晩ご飯はカレーです
examplePolite.english: Tonight's dinner is curry.

example.romaji: kaeri ni raamen tabete kanai?
example.ja: 帰りにラーメン食べてかない?
example.english: Want to grab ramen on the way home?

examplePolite.romaji: kaeri ni raamen o tabete ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 帰りにラーメンを食べていきませんか?
examplePolite.english: Would you like to get ramen on the way home?

example.romaji: oiwai da kara sushi tabe ni ikou
example.ja: お祝いだから寿司食べに行こう
example.english: It's a celebration, let's go for sushi.

examplePolite.romaji: oiwai na node sushi o tabe ni ikimashou
examplePolite.ja: お祝いなので寿司を食べに行きましょう
examplePolite.english: Since it's a celebration, let's go out for sushi.

notes: Often said osushi. Kaitenzushi is conveyor-belt sushi.

example.romaji: kaze no toki wa udon ga ii yo
example.ja: 風邪の時はうどんがいいよ
example.english: Udon is good when you've got a cold.

examplePolite.romaji: kaze no toki wa udon ga ii desu yo
examplePolite.ja: 風邪の時はうどんがいいですよ
examplePolite.english: Udon is good when you have a cold.

use: The group you're in at school, not a single lesson; a lesson is jugyou.

example.romaji: onaji kurasu datta yo ne?
example.ja: 同じクラスだったよね?
example.english: We were in the same class, right?

examplePolite.romaji: onaji kurasu deshita yo ne?
examplePolite.ja: 同じクラスでしたよね?
examplePolite.english: We were in the same class, weren't we?

notes: Also a level or grade, as in hai kurasu (high-end).

use: Used for finishing any level of school, not just university.

example.romaji: rainen daigaku sotsugyou suru n da
example.ja: 来年大学卒業するんだ
example.english: I graduate from university next year.

examplePolite.romaji: rainen daigaku o sotsugyou shimasu
examplePolite.ja: 来年大学を卒業します
examplePolite.english: I'll graduate from university next year.

notes: Takes o: daigaku o sotsugyou suru. Sotsugyoushiki is the graduation ceremony; also used for leaving a group or growing out of a habit.

use: Mostly a school sports or hobby club, named by its activity, like sakkaa bu (soccer club).

example.romaji: bu no renshuu ga mainichi aru n da
example.ja: 部の練習が毎日あるんだ
example.english: We have club practice every day.

examplePolite.romaji: bu no renshuu ga mainichi aru n desu
examplePolite.ja: 部の練習が毎日あるんです
examplePolite.english: We have club practice every day.

notes: Bukatsu is club activities. In a company it means a department, like eigyoubu (sales).

english: qualification; licence; the right (to do something)

example.romaji: shigoto no tame ni shikaku torou to omotte
example.ja: 仕事のために資格取ろうと思って
example.english: I'm thinking of getting a qualification for work.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto no tame ni shikaku o torou to omotte imasu
examplePolite.ja: 仕事のために資格を取ろうと思っています
examplePolite.english: I'm planning to get a qualification for my job.

notes: Shikaku o toru means get a qualification. Iu shikaku nai means you have no right to say that.

example.romaji: kono aji chotto usukunai?
example.ja: この味ちょっと薄くない?
example.english: Isn't this a bit bland?

examplePolite.romaji: kono aji, chotto usukunai desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: この味、ちょっと薄くないですか?
examplePolite.english: Isn't the flavour a little weak?

notes: Aji ga koi is strong-tasting, aji ga usui mild or bland. Nan no aji? asks what flavour it is.

use: Raw food, a draft beer at a bar, or something seen live and in person.

example.romaji: kore nama de taberareru no?
example.ja: これ生で食べられるの?
example.english: Can you eat this raw?

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa nama de taberaremasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: これは生で食べられますか?
examplePolite.english: Can this be eaten raw?

notes: Toriaezu nama is the classic bar order: a draft beer to start. Nama de mita means saw it live.

example.romaji: gomen, soko no shio totte
example.ja: ごめん、そこの塩取って
example.english: Sorry, can you pass me the salt?

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, soko no shio o totte kudasai
examplePolite.ja: すみません、そこの塩を取ってください
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, could you pass the salt?

example.romaji: shouyu kakesugi ja nai?
example.ja: 醤油かけすぎじゃない?
example.english: Isn't that too much soy sauce?

examplePolite.romaji: shouyu o kakesugi ja nai desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 醤油をかけすぎじゃないですか?
examplePolite.english: Aren't you putting on too much soy sauce?

notes: Shouyu o kakeru is pour it on; shouyu ni tsukeru is dip in it.
